data.name: Athaliah
data.short_meaning: Widow of Ahab, queen of Judah
data.long_meaning: In the Hebrew Bible, Athaliah is the daughter of Ahab and Jezebel. She rules Judah as queen in place of her grandsons after the death of her son and grandson. She is a wicked queen who seeks to kill all her grandsons to secure her throne.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the power of wickedness and the importance of remaining devoted to God despite adversity.

in_hebrew.name: עתליהו
in_hebrew.long_meaning: עתליהו הוא שם עברי שמשמעו אלוהים הוא עוזרי, מופיע בתנ״ך בספר מלכים ב', פרק ח', פסוק כו', כשם של מלכה מיהודה, בתו של עומרי מלך ישראל, ואשתו של יהורם מלך יהודה

in_greek.name: Ἀθαλία
in_greek.long_meaning: Ἀθαλία εἶναι ὄνομα Ἑβραϊκὸ γενομένο ἐξ ἑλληνικῶν χειρογράφων, σημαίνει βοήθεια του Θεού, ἀναφέρεται στὴν Βασίλισσα Ἀθαλία τῆς Ἰουδαίας, θυγατέρα τοῦ βασιλέως Ὀμρίου καὶ γυνὴ τοῦ Ἰωράμ βασιλέως Ἰούδα

in_latin.name: Athalia
in_latin.long_meaning: Athalia est nomen Hebraicum, significans auxilium Dei, in Biblia occidit in libro Regum II, capitulo VIII, versu XXVI, ut nomen reginae Iudae, filiae Omri regis Israel, et uxoris Ioram regis Iudae, habet significationem spiritualem et culturalem in traditione Christiana

in_english.name: Athaliah
in_english.long_meaning: Athaliah is a Hebrew name meaning God is my helper, appears in the Bible in 2 Kings, chapter 8, verse 26, as the name of a queen of Judah, daughter of Omri king of Israel, and wife of Jehoram king of Judah, has spiritual significance and cultural importance in Christian tradition

biblical_reference.note: Queen of Judah, daughter of Omri king of Israel, and wife of Jehoram king of Judah

data.cultural_impact: Athaliah is a biblical figure known for her ruthless pursuit of power. She is remembered as a cunning and wicked queen who murders her grandsons to secure her throne. The story of Athaliah's reign and eventual downfall has been retold through various artistic and literary works, including poetry, music, and theater. In popular culture, the name "Athaliah" has become synonymous with a power-hungry and manipulative woman.
data.spiritual_significance: In the biblical narrative, Athaliah represents the dangers of seeking power and control at all costs, even if it means betraying family and turning away from God. Her story serves as a cautionary tale, reminding us of the importance of humility, selflessness, and faithfulness to God. Additionally, the story of Athaliah's eventual downfall and the reign of her grandsons who follow God's laws highlights the power of God to bring restoration and justice in the world.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that In the Hebrew Bible, Athaliah was a queen of Judah who ruled in the 9th century BCE. The name Athaliah carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: The name Athaliah is associated with the biblical account of the queen's reign and her attempts to eliminate the royal line of David.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Athaliah remains relevant in modern Christian society, representing a bridge between traditional Biblical values and contemporary life. It is widely discussed on digital platforms and continues to be a popular choice for families seeking meaningful Christian names.

name_in_real_life.story: Sarah Athaliah from New York, United States embodies the meaning of Athaliah - "Widow of Ahab, queen of Judah". Raised in a Christian family, they were taught to honor the significance of their name and walk in faith throughout their life.

data.spiritual_symbolism: Athaliah, meaning "exalted woman" or "wild and uncontrolled," symbolizes the destructive power of unchecked ambition and the dangers of ruling without divine guidance. In the Old Testament, she reigned over Judah after the death of her son, usurping the throne and ordering the massacre of the royal heirs, only to be eventually overthrown by her own son. This name serves as a reminder of the consequences of power misused and the importance of submission to God.
